elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: 19.1 (retained): "Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form."

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: 19.1: "Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications"; amended 19.2: "each Deliverable and any software will materially conform to its documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Amended 19.2 sets the conformance period at "ninety days after delivery or first availability", not twelve months. To reach preferred the drafter must state a 12-month software conformance period.

19.1 warrants Services performance and conformance with no expiry, and the amendment deletes the former cut-off in 19.2 ("after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation"), so no limit shorter than 90 days remains.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: 19.4 (retained): "Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge."
19.4: "Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: The rationale asserts Section 19.3 covers Applicable Law, but 19.3 was not supplied among the cited or rendered paragraphs, so its operative wording cannot be verified here. Preferred fails regardless on the 12-month element.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: Same position: malicious-code coverage is attributed to unquoted Section 19.3; no rendered operative text confirms scope (Services and Deliverables) or wording.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Amended 19.2: "For ninety days after delivery or first availability, each Deliverable and any software will materially conform to its documentation." The deterministic period check returned false only because the duration is spelled in words ("ninety") rather than numerals; in substance it equals the 90-day floor, and "or first availability" correctly anchors hosted software that is not physically delivered.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: 19.1 warrants Services performance and material conformance with no stated expiry; with the 19.2 cut-off sentence deleted, nothing truncates the Services warranty below 30 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: 19.4: "promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge", expressly triggered by breach of Sections 19.1 or 19.2.
19.4: "Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it" where cure is not achieved within a reasonable period.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: 19.2 as amended gives a ninety-day documentation-conformance warranty expressly extended to software, 19.1 supplies an untimed Services warranty (well beyond the 30-day floor), and 19.4 supplies repair/replace and refund remedies keyed to both 19.1 and 19.2.

Preferred is not reached: the software conformance period is ninety days rather than twelve months, and the compliance-with-laws and no-malicious-code elements sit in an unquoted Section 19.3 that cannot be verified from the rendered text. This is correctly pressed only to the fallback and noted in the comment.

Minimality holds. The edit touches only 19.2: the period (fifteen to ninety days), the covered items (adding software alongside Deliverables), and deletion of the cut-off sentence. The deleted words ("after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation") are Vendor-favourable and directly extinguish the checklist remedies, including remedies for the otherwise untimed 19.1 Services warranty, so their removal is necessary rather than cosmetic. No survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories, or boilerplate was added.

Intent preserved: the 19.4 cross-reference to "Section 19.1 or 19.2" still resolves, the non-exclusive remedy carve-out for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims survives intact, and no retained sentence now contradicts the ninety-day period or leaves an undefined term.

Deterministic evidence reviewed in substance: the failed "period ≥ 90 days" check is a numeral-matching artifact ("ninety days"), not a genuine shortfall; the operation, minimality, and coverage gates all pass.

Optional polish (not required for the fallback): if pressing further, ask for twelve months on software conformance and quote 19.3 to confirm the Applicable Law and malicious-code warranties cover both Services and Deliverables.
